final_trustworthiness_assessment:
High overall trustworthiness:
• CDC sources (cdc.gov) are the gold standard for US measles surveillance — HAN advisory and MMWR reports are peer-reviewed or officially cleared.
• Texas DSHS (dshs.texas.gov) is the primary state authority — press releases referenced in snippets are authoritative for TX-specific case counts and deaths.
• New Mexico DOH (nmhealth.org) is the primary state authority for NM data — the 2025 Measles Outbreak sub-page is present in the candidate set.
• PAHO (paho.org, 4 results) provides independent international validation.
• CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu) is a highly regarded academic public health news outlet that consistently cites CDC as its primary source — suitable as a secondary corroborator.
• Texas Tribune (texastribune.org) explicitly states it used DSHS data from January–June 2025 — high credibility for TX-specific figures.
• Lubbock Online (lubbockonline.com) is a local outlet with direct access to Lubbock Public Health — suitable for locality-level detail.
• Wikipedia is useful for narrative and locality identification but numeric fields must be traced to primary sources.
• ArcGIS dashboard (arcgis.com) — the NM Lea County death snippet (3/6/25) is useful but the dashboard is a secondary aggregator; the nmhealth.org page is the preferred primary source for NM data.
• YouTube videos cannot yield evidence_quote extractions and should be deprioritized.
• Facebook result should be excluded as non-authoritative.
